newsitem.title: USA: Probe continues into Cohen shooting in Maine.
newsitem.headline: Probe continues into Cohen shooting in Maine.

text.p: Investigators Friday worked to sort through differing accounts of a shooting by the brother of Defence Secretary William Cohen.

Family and friends of Robert Cohen said he had been harassed repeatedly by Michael Chasse and was acting in self defence when he fired his gun Tuesday evening, wounding Chasse, the Portland Press Herald reported.
The Bangor Daily News said Cohen had recently filed a police report against Chasse, who has a criminal record for terrorising and assault and is under indictment for burglarly and other charges.
Chasse, recovering from a neck wound at a Bangor hospital, told reporters he went to Cohen's home Tuesday as a friend and disputed accusations that he attacked Cohen with a knife.
Pennobscot County District Attorney Christopher Almy said he expected criminal charges would be filed but authorities Friday refused to say if Cohen, 51, or Chasse, 22, likely would face prosecution.

Cohen's supporters said Chasse, who was also a friend of Cohen's daughter, had for several weeks tried to intimidate Cohen with demands for money and Cohen had expressed a fear for his life, the newspapers reported.
"Bobby Cohen has been through hell," Bobby Russell, a long-time friend, told the Press Herald.
Cohen, who is the defence secretary's younger brother, had a permit for the small-calibre handgun used in the shooting.
